subject: Audit every graded lab for finishStage double-completion
description:
ModuleProgress.complete() is not idempotent: it increments the lifetime modules-completed counter, calls updateStreak(), queues an activity event and shows the overlay. Labs whose task ticks are deliberately revocable (recomputed by evaluate) can re-enable their finish button after credit was already awarded, so pressing Finish again double-awards. Found by Nancy 2026-08-07 on ch25 forge-virtualization.lab.html, fixed there with a sticky LAB.completed flag persisted as completedOnce. Any lab sharing the evaluate/finishStage shape likely has the same gap; ch25 was simply the one where a rename feature made it easy to reach. Sweep the other .lab.html files that call ModuleProgress.complete from a re-evaluable button.
[2026-08-08 03:57] SWEPT + FIXED in 1791137dd, but NOT the way the task assumed. Built _tools/eduscan/finish-double-award-audit.js (validated both directions against ch25 pre-fix and post-fix from git history). It found 589 call sites across 592 lab files; only 19 have a sticky guard. 15 are RECOMPUTED (inside render/update fns -- award re-fires on every call with no second click), 326 HANDLER, 227 UNGUARDED. Patching 570 labs would be one fix written 570 times, so the fix went into ModuleProgress.complete(): the lifetime counter is now gated on isFirstCompletion, the flag the function already computed and already used for pushToUserProfile. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS TASK: updateStreak() was already same-day idempotent so it was never a harm; and complete() is still NOT fully idempotent (overlay + re-sync still fire) -- only the cumulative, unrecoverable counter effect is fixed. ALSO fixed a pre-existing bug this depended on: reset() never cleared completedModules/completionCounts, so reset-then-redo awarded no XP, and gating the counter on that array would have made the counter unrestorable after a reset. 12/12 in _tools/eduscan/moduleprogress-idempotency.test.js against the real component in a vm sandbox; 5 of those fail on the pre-fix code.
